=== ITEM 1, THE HANDOFF'S TOP ITEM: DETERMINISM. CLOSED. ===

REPRODUCED BEFORE ANY FIX (rule 4). street|day and well|day differ across three back-to-back captures with identical arguments and nothing touched between them. street: 7 differing 16-bit samples of 128000, first at 0.5833 s. well: 61-65, first at 0.235 s. Max 1 LSB. market, writ_house, barge_hold, dungeon, interior bit-identical in the same run.

1 LSB IS A FACT ABOUT THE QUANTISER, NOT THE RENDERER, so I measured the float domain: street diverges by 2.98e-8 (-150.5 dBFS) on 30313 of 64000 samples from sample 0; well by 1.64e-7. That excludes a scheduling divergence (order 1e-1, late) and points at arithmetic.

LOCALISED (D3): the continuous bed, not the events. well is unstable with L1 ALONE (a four-partial drone). street is stable with L1 alone AND with L2 alone, and unstable only once all three continuous layers are present. Two beds, and the ladder said they were two different shapes of the same thing.

ROOT CAUSE, PROVED OUTSIDE OUR CODE BEFORE A LINE CHANGED (rule 10). D0 renders bare OscillatorNode/GainNode graphs with no Elder Souls code in them: 1 source into one node IDENTICAL, 2 IDENTICAL, 3 DIVERGES 1.49e-8, 8 DIVERGES 4.47e-8. One and two are exact because IEEE-754 addition is commutative and x+0 is x. Three breaks because addition is NOT ASSOCIATIVE. The platform sums a node's inputs in an order the graph does not fix; the difference is one float32 ULP.

IT IS INTERMITTENT, which is why two rounds of gates walked past it: in one control run the 4-source case diverged, in the next it was clean, same commit, same browser. A single green from a flat topology is worth nothing, and no check before this one repeated a render at all.

REMEDY TESTED IN THE CONTROL BEFORE BEING WRITTEN INTO THE SYNTHESISER: the same D0 probe's `chained` arm (no node over two connections) is IDENTICAL at n = 1, 2, 3, 4, 8 on every run. Two arms of one probe on one tree disagreeing is what says the topology is the mechanism.

FIX: DeterministicMixer + joinChain in synth.js. Everywhere three or more signals met, they now meet two at a time in an order the graph fixes — the drone chord's partials, a grain's oscillator partials, a grain's repeats (roof_rat is six taps 0.09 s apart with a 0.10 s decay, so they really do overlap), and the ambience bus, now a fixed ladder of 16 lanes (twice RI-AUD02 SecD V5's eight-voice cap). Continuous voices reserve a lane; grains rotate. Reservations reset on a region swap so the outgoing and incoming generations share a lane across the 4 s crossfade — two simultaneously sounding signals in one node, which is exact.

COST IS AT MOST ONE ULP. street's post-fix digest equals one of the two orderings it was already producing, i.e. the fix PINNED the render rather than altering it. Nothing this project reports has that precision, so no calibrated number was invalidated.
ACCEPTANCE, HEADLINE RE-TAKEN AT HEAD 0f6ff17 AFTER HEAD MOVED FOUR TIMES: all 20 beds x 2 tod x 3 captures BIT-IDENTICAL. D0, D1, D2, D3 all PASS.

DELETE-THE-FIX (rule 6), same tree, same commit, nothing staged (rule 17): __ES_AUDIO_FLAT_MIX restores flat N-input summation at every site the fix chained. 8 OF 20 BEDS go red — crimson-coast, deep-marshes, eastern-rootlands, street, well, stone-forest, valus-ridge, western-rootlands. THE TWO ARMS DIFFER: 0 of 40 as shipped, 8 of 20 with the fix deleted.

ROUND 2 SAW TWO OF THE EIGHT, AND THEY WERE NOT THE IMPORTANT ONES. Six of the eight are REGION beds, which is what every B1/B2/B3 pack is built from; valus-ridge is the worst at 3.28e-7. The two interiors round 2 found were simply the ones that happened to tip a rounding boundary on the day it measured. That is why the fix had to be topological rather than a patch to two bed files.

MY OWN DELETE-THE-FIX ARM WAS HALF AN ARM AT FIRST and I am recording it because it nearly shipped as a pass. It gated only the bus ladder: street went red and well stayed GREEN, because well's half of the defect is the four-partial chord, still chained. The flag now covers both sites.
SENSITIVITY ARM: --sabotage gain leaks Math.random()*0.01 dB into the master trim between captures; all beds tested go red at 3-6 LSB. D1 catches an unseeded quantity ~40 dB below anything audible.
THE TOOL THAT RAISED THE FLAG IN ROUND 2, RUN UNCHANGED, IS NOW GREEN: ambience-interior-consumption I1/I2/I3 all PASS, `restored=true` for all seven interiors including street and well.
=== ITEM 2: B5 / THE 'REGRESSION' ROUND 2 DECLARED. CLOSED, AND IT WAS NOT A REGRESSION. ===
REPRODUCED FIRST on the round-1 critic's own instrument run unchanged: C_B5_strict 11/13, clay-moor -31.818 against its own target of -26, deep-marshes -28.003.
BUT ambience-render measured the same clay-moor bed at -24.66. SEVEN DECIBELS between two instruments on one bed. That gap, not the trim, was the finding.

MECHANISM, MEASURED NOT ASSUMED: clay-moor's kiln is a CONTINUOUS R7 emitter at pos [3743,2010], audible_m 520. ambience-render teleports the player into the region first, so the kiln is in earshot and adds 5.6 dB RMS; the critic probe does not teleport and captures from the default position 3.1 km away, where the kiln contributes nothing. Directly measured: bed alone -27.234 RMS, listener at the kiln -21.661. Round 2 CALIBRATED with the kiln in and the gate MEASURED it out. Not a drift — the calibration target and the gate disagreed about whether a landmark is part of the bed.

RULING, AND IT IS THE UNCOMFORTABLE ONE: an emitter's level is by construction a function of where you stand (that is all of R7, and B6 asserts it), so it belongs to B6 and not to B5. bed_gain_db is now calibrated AND gated on the bed without landmarks; the spectrum keeps its emitters because SecC's key separates four regions by them. NOTE THIS READING MAKES CLAY-MOOR FAIL WHERE THE AMBIGUOUS ONE PASSED — it was not chosen because it was comfortable, and it needed a real recalibration to satisfy. The item's silence on the point is referred as AMENDMENT-W1-22-01 item C.

deep-marshes bed_lufs_target -28 -> -27.5. -28 is the exact bottom edge of B5's band and the bed landed 0.003 outside it. Same defect and same remedy round 2 applied to marauders-coast (-24 -> -24.5) and left half-done; deep-marshes was the other fence-target. THE BAND IS UNCHANGED and nothing is loosened.

NEW GATE G4b_level_strict in the BUILDER's tool: B5 verbatim, absolute -28..-24, Stone Wastes exempt at -34+-2. It existed only in the critic's probe, and a gate a piece only ever fails in someone else's instrument is a gate the piece does not have. G4's +-4 LU window passed 13/13 through the whole clay-moor mis-calibration.

RESULT ON THE CRITIC'S OWN INSTRUMENT, RUN UNCHANGED: C_B5_strict 13/13, out_of_band []. B5 is closed — the round-1 verdict scored it 12/13 and round 2 left it at 11/13. Worst residual at 20 s is valus-ridge 0.71 LU from its own target, well inside the band.

=== ITEM 3: O3, THE EVENT LEVELS. CLOSED, AND THE FIRST FIX WAS WRONG. ===
Round 2 handed off clay-moor L3 +4.91, clay-moor L4 +9.56, stone-forest L4 -9.37 as 'calibration convergence — one more --calibrate pass would pull them in'. It would not.

FIRST PASS: --calibrate then re-measure. 18 of 20 beds landed EXACTLY on target and stone-forest/L4 went -9.76 -> 0. CLAY-MOOR DID NOT MOVE AT ALL: its trim was cut 6.91 dB and the measurement changed by 0.05 dB. A trim that large moving nothing means the measured quantity is not a function of the trim — a falsification of the measurement, not a stubborn bed.

CAUSE 1: the bed reference muted 'R7' wholesale, removing clay-moor's CONTINUOUS kiln from the reference while leaving it in the mix, so the residual was the kiln's roar. emitterMode() already made that distinction and the mute vocabulary did not carry it. Added R7_strike / R7_continuous; EVENT_MUTE is now ['L3','L4','R7_strike'].

THAT WAS NECESSARY AND NOT SUFFICIENT, and only the new control found the rest. CAUSE 2: renderBedOffline built the emitters from the SAME Rng the event scheduler draws from, and after it — so muting the event layers changed how many draws had been consumed and rendered a DIFFERENT kiln in the muted pass. The subtraction's founding promise, 'the bed cancels to the sample', was false for any bed with a rendered emitter. Fixed with emitterRng(seedBase, i), a per-SLOT stream so a mute that skips one emitter cannot shift the next, derived from the bed seed so _swapLive() and renderBedOffline() build the same kiln (this file's founding rule).

NEW GATE O4_level_tracks_trim + --sabotage trimshift: move every event_gain_db by a known -6 dB and require every bed's MEASURED level to follow. THIS IS THE CHECK O3 WAS MISSING AND ITS ABSENCE COST A ROUND — a gate on a level needs a gate on the level RESPONDING, or a broken instrument reads as a stubborn bed. First run: 38 of 40 tracked to within 0.01 dB, clay-moor moved 0.00. After the emitter-RNG fix: 40 of 40, MAX ERROR 0.06 dB.

WITH THE MEASUREMENT REPAIRED, clay-moor's true event level was -17.57 dB rel bed, not the +4.9 it had reported for two rounds. Recalibrated. O3_level_in_band PASSES, and it has held across three independent non-calibrating runs.

Three clips of 40 still produce nothing a detector can pick out: salt-hills/day, salt-hills/night, market/night. salt-hills' L3 layer is named l3_legion_horn but its only scheduled event is dry_grass_gust (attack 0.45 s, decay 1.2 s) — the horn itself is an R7 emitter on a 3600 s period. market's L3 crate_down is a 210 Hz bandpass under a broadband crowd bed and sits below the detector's 300 Hz highpass. I did NOT widen the detector again to catch them: round 2 already widened it once after seeing an acceptance result, and doing it twice would be tuning the instrument to the answer. Both look like real acoustic facts about those two beds rather than detector defects, but I did not have the budget to prove that, and I am not claiming it.

It is referred as AMENDMENT-W1-22-01 item A with the arithmetic: measured median bed-only crest 12.3 dB, full-mix 16.2 dB, 3 of 40 clips reach the judge's 20 dB. Reaching 20 needs the events 6-8 dB outside SecA's -6..+2 / -4..+4. notes_for_successor: The determinism fix is TOPOLOGICAL and lives in synth.js. Anything that adds a new place where three signals meet must route through DeterministicMixer/joinChain or it silently reopens the defect, and it will not show up reliably because the fault is intermittent. tools/analysis/ambience-determinism.mjs is the fence — run it, and run --sabotage flatmix occasionally to confirm it can still go red. Likewise: never trust an event-level number from ambience-onsets without O4; --sabotage trimshift is one run and it is the difference between a measurement and a plausible number.
